title: The Holes by Max Wolf Friedlich at The Wild Project #theholesplay #ma...
transcript: I was super intrigued to see this follow-up play from the team behind the hit thriller Job, and it was equally captivating but much stranger. Initially, it presents as a combination of two familiar premises, one being a small town where an outsider comes in, another being a long-standing community institution with some secret that nobody talks about, but everyone knows. It's more stylistically ambiguous than Job, packing tone shifts rather than plot twists, especially once we get past the exposition-heavy first act. Through a pretty funny story that feels equally real and fantastical, a couple of themes naturally emerge, such as masculinity and gentrification. I wouldn't say that a particular argument comes into view. There's plenty to interpret here, and the piece feels robust with its well-defined characters, strong performances, and tight scene work. One way it does resemble Job is in its calculated flow of information, which keeps you leaning in from start to finish. The enigmatic ending doesn't quite stick the landing, though in retrospect, I'm not sure how well it could ever be resolved. But for me, this didn't make it any less of an enjoyable watch. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Reviewer finds the play captivating, funny, and robust with strong performances, though notes the ending doesn't quite stick the landing. Clear recommendation with modest caveats.
